pins.title: District office hosted a Senior Scam Stopper seminar at the Redwood City Public Library
pins.summary: Senator Becker's office hosted an in-person Senior Scam Stopper seminar in the community room of the Redwood City Public Library. Speakers from the California Department of Insurance, the Department of Financial Protection and Innovation, the California Privacy Protection Agency, and the Contractors State License Board covered insurance fraud, identity theft, phone scams, and repair scams. The seminar was aimed at helping older residents recognize and avoid common scams.

pins.title: District office staffed a constituent help table at the Coastside Farmers' Market
pins.summary: Senator Becker's district office staff set up a constituent help table at the Coastside Farmers' Market at Shoreline Station in Half Moon Bay. Staff answered questions and helped residents navigate state programs and resolve issues with state agencies. It was one stop in a series of farmers' market visits across the district.

pins.title: District office staffed a constituent help table at the California Avenue Farmers' Market
pins.summary: Senator Becker's district office staff set up a constituent help table at the California Avenue Farmers' Market in Palo Alto. Staff answered constituent questions and helped residents connect with state programs and agencies. It was one stop in a series of farmers' market visits across the district.

pins.title: Spoke at a Martin Luther King, Jr. Day of Service event in Foster City
pins.summary: Senator Becker spoke at the Peninsula Multifaith Coalition's Day of Service at the Peninsula Jewish Community Center in Foster City on Martin Luther King, Jr. Day. The event was one of several service events he joined across the district that day.

pins.title: Authored SB 968, signed into law, making free community college permanent in San Mateo County
pins.location_name: San Mateo County Community College District
pins.summary: Senator Becker authored SB 968, signed into law in June 2026, which deleted the 2028 expiration date from the free-tuition program he created with SB 893 in 2022. That makes tuition-free community college permanent for qualifying students at the San Mateo County Community College District — Cañada College, College of San Mateo and Skyline College. His office says the pilot has helped more than 35,000 students and raised district enrollment by 24 percent.

pins.title: $1.5 million secured to renovate the Community Services Agency's Mountain View headquarters
pins.location_name: Community Services Agency (CSA) of Mountain View
pins.summary: Senator Becker secured $1.5 million in state funding to renovate the Mountain View headquarters of the Community Services Agency of Mountain View, Los Altos and Los Altos Hills, which serves more than 6,000 residents. The renovated headquarters expanded the food pantry and modernized the building, and reopened with a ribbon-cutting in 2025.

pins.title: $2 million helped complete East Palo Alto's first regulation football field
pins.location_name: East Palo Alto regulation football field
pins.summary: As Bay Area Caucus chair, Becker helped secure the final $2 million needed to complete East Palo Alto's first regulation-size football field, a roughly $4 million community project that broke ground in September 2025.

pins.title: 200 laptops distributed to East Palo Alto students to close the digital divide
pins.location_name: East Palo Alto laptop distribution (with AT&T, StreetCode Academy, Human-I-T)
pins.summary: In 2025, Senator Becker worked with AT&T, StreetCode Academy, and Human-I-T to distribute 200 laptops to East Palo Alto students and families. The aim was to help close the digital divide, so students without a computer at home aren't left behind on schoolwork or job applications.

pins.title: Celebrated 10 years of the Genentech–South San Francisco schools STEM partnership
pins.summary: Senator Becker joined educators, community leaders, and Genentech employees in South San Francisco to celebrate the 10th anniversary of Futurelab. The program is a long-running partnership between Genentech and the South San Francisco Unified School District that gives local students hands-on STEM education.

pins.title: Launched emergency food drive for families facing SNAP loss
pins.summary: In response to a federal government shutdown that threatened SNAP/CalFresh benefits, Senator Becker's district office launched an emergency food drive, collecting non-perishable donations weekdays. Donations collected by his staff were delivered to local food banks to support families in Senate District 13.

pins.title: Named Olga Melo the Senate District 13 2025 Woman of the Year
pins.summary: Senator Becker named Mountain View community leader Olga Melo the 2025 Woman of the Year for Senate District 13 and honored her on the Senate floor as part of the California Legislative Women's Caucus ceremony. The recognition celebrated her work on tenants' rights, public health, and civic engagement, including co-founding the Community Action Team and helping pass Mountain View's Measure V rent control.

pins.title: Held a community coffee with residents at the Burlingame Community Center
pins.summary: Senator Becker held a "Java with Josh" community coffee at the Burlingame Community Center, joined by Burlingame Mayor Peter Stevenson. The informal event gave residents a chance to hear what he was working on in the Legislature and raise local concerns directly. It was one in a series of community coffees he held around the Peninsula.

pins.title: Held a community coffee with residents at Chit Chat Cafe in Pacifica
pins.summary: Senator Becker held a "Java with Josh" community coffee at Chit Chat Cafe in Pacifica, joined by Pacifica Mayor Sue Beckmeyer. Residents were invited to hear about his legislative work and share what was on their minds. It was part of a series of community coffees held across the district.

pins.title: Joined local leaders in Redwood City at a public event supporting public schools
pins.summary: Senator Becker joined Congressman Kevin Mullin, other elected officials, and education leaders at 500 County Center in Redwood City for a public event supporting local public education. The event was organized around the federal order to close the U.S. Department of Education and what it could mean for California students. Attendees were invited to share concerns about special education, school meals, civil rights protections, and student loans.

pins.title: Called on Caltrans to fix a hazardous wet stretch near the Highway 92 summit
pins.summary: Senator Becker, Assemblymember Marc Berman and Supervisor Ray Mueller publicly called on Caltrans to address a hazardous stretch near the Highway 92 summit, where a natural spring wets the pavement. Caltrans reported in May 2025 that it had diverted the water and installed warning signs. The officials said a permanent fix was still needed.

pins.title: Held constituent office hours at the Los Gatos Farmers' Market
pins.location_name: Los Gatos Farmers' Market, Town Plaza Park
pins.summary: Senator Becker and his staff set up at the Los Gatos Farmers' Market to answer residents' questions and help them navigate state programs. It was part of a run of farmers' market office hours he held across the district.

pins.title: Helped secure the state funding that supports the Colma Creek Adaptation Project
pins.summary: Senator Becker helped double the state's coastal and bayside flood protection funding, and his office's announcement names the Colma Creek Adaptation Project in South San Francisco as one of the projects that pot supports. The release does not state how much of the money went to Colma Creek, so no dollar figure is claimed here. The project uses nature-based methods to strengthen flood defenses while improving habitat.

pins.title: Authored SB 338, the farmworker telehealth law co-sponsored by Half Moon Bay's ALAS
pins.summary: Senator Becker authored SB 338, signed into law in October 2025, which expands mobile telehealth for farmworkers. The bill was co-sponsored by Half Moon Bay's Ayudando Latinos A Sonar (ALAS) and is modeled on the ALAS Farmworker Equity Express, a mobile clinic that rotates among farms in the afternoons and evenings when workers are available. The program itself deploys virtual health hubs in two rural communities that the law does not name.

pins.title: Authored SB 272, signed into law, to speed up SamTrans construction contracting
pins.location_name: San Mateo County Transit District (SamTrans) headquarters
pins.summary: Senator Becker authored SB 272, signed into law in October 2025, letting the San Mateo County Transit District — SamTrans — use job order contracting, a faster way to hire contractors for routine repair and maintenance work. The pilot caps any single job order at $1 million and runs through 2032, and the district must report back to the Legislature by 2030. SamTrans runs the county's bus system from its headquarters in San Carlos.

pins.title: Authored SB 390, signed into law, easing shoreline development in South San Francisco
pins.location_name: South San Francisco East of 101 area
pins.summary: Senator Becker authored SB 390, signed into law in October 2025, working with the South San Francisco city council. The law removes a landowner-consent requirement that had made it harder to add shoreline land in San Mateo County to a community facilities district — a tool local governments use to pay for infrastructure. Becker said the aim was to make economic development easier in South San Francisco east of Highway 101.

pins.title: $2 million secured for a permanent Black History Museum
pins.summary: Becker negotiated $2 million in state funds to help the Domini Hoskins Black History Museum move from a pop-up to a permanent home. He presented the funding to the museum's leaders in Redwood City in February 2024.

pins.title: State funding restored for the Burlingame Broadway rail crossing
pins.summary: Becker helped lead 2024 budget negotiations that restored $150 million to a state rail program after it was cut, keeping funding on track for priority Peninsula grade-separation projects — including Burlingame's Broadway crossing, long ranked among California's most dangerous.

pins.title: State funding restored for the Mountain View Caltrain crossing
pins.location_name: Mountain View Caltrain Grade Separation Project
pins.summary: Becker helped lead 2024 budget negotiations that restored $150 million to a state rail program after a proposed cut, keeping priority Peninsula grade-separation projects — including Mountain View's Caltrain crossing — eligible to move toward construction and draw federal matching funds.

pins.title: State funding restored for Palo Alto's rail grade separation
pins.location_name: Connecting Palo Alto Rail Grade Separation Project
pins.summary: Becker helped lead 2024 budget negotiations that restored $150 million to a state rail program after a proposed cut, keeping the Connecting Palo Alto grade-separation project eligible for state funding and federal matching dollars.

pins.title: Lutticken's Deli named Senate District 13 Small Business of the Year
pins.summary: Senator Becker named Lutticken's Deli & After 5 Restaurant his 2024 Small Business of the Year. The longtime Menlo Park family business is known for donating food to local veterans, sponsoring youth sports, and feeding people in need during the pandemic.

pins.title: Move Mountain View named Senate District 13 Nonprofit of the Year
pins.summary: Senator Becker named Move Mountain View his 2024 Nonprofit of the Year. The group addresses homelessness with safe overnight parking, services, and hygiene facilities for residents living in their vehicles.

pins.title: Hosted a Senior Scam Stopper seminar at the San Mateo Main Library
pins.summary: Senator Becker and Assemblymember Diane Papan hosted a Senior Scam Stopper seminar in the Oak Room of the San Mateo Main Library. Speakers from the San Mateo Police Department, the Health Insurance Counseling and Advocacy Program of San Mateo, and the Contractors State License Board covered internet scams, Medicare fraud, and home improvement schemes. The seminar walked seniors through how to spot these scams and what to check before hiring a contractor.

pins.title: Held a community coffee with residents at Redwood City City Hall
pins.summary: Senator Becker held a "Java with Josh" community coffee at Redwood City City Hall, joined by Redwood City Mayor Jeff Gee. The informal gathering was part of a Peninsula-wide series where residents could hear about his legislative work and raise local concerns.

pins.title: Took part in a Hillsborough town hall on the home insurance crisis
pins.summary: Senator Becker joined a town hall in Hillsborough on the cost and availability of home insurance in wildfire-risk areas. He spoke about his proposal to have insurers credit homeowners who reduce their own wildfire risk through steps such as clearing defensible space around a house. The source does not name the venue, so the pin sits at Hillsborough Town Hall.

pins.title: Helped present the Hillsborough Citizen of the Year and Community Care Awards
pins.summary: Senator Becker joined the Hillsborough City School District's parent group to honor its Citizen of the Year and Community Care Award recipients. Lisa Edwards was named Citizen of the Year and former Superintendent Dr. Louann Carlomagno received the Community Care Award.

pins.title: Took part in a discussion at Stanford University on clean energy
pins.summary: Senator Becker hosted the U.S. Department of Energy's loan programs director on a visit to Stanford and took part in a public conversation there on how the country can move to clean energy. The visit was aimed at connecting California clean-technology businesses with federal support. No building was named in the source, so the pin sits at the campus center.

pins.title: $2 million secured for farmworker & senior housing in Half Moon Bay
pins.summary: Senator Becker secured $2 million in the state budget to help build affordable housing for Half Moon Bay's farmworker and senior residents. The funds support the Senior and Farmworker Housing project at 555 Kelly Avenue.

pins.title: $1 million secured for senior affordable housing in North Fair Oaks
pins.location_name: Alta Housing North Fair Oaks Senior Housing Project
pins.summary: Becker secured $1 million in the 2023 state budget for pre-development costs of Alta Housing's North Fair Oaks senior affordable housing project, to be built on land the nonprofit already owns in the North Fair Oaks area near Redwood City.

pins.title: $300,000 secured for park and community projects in Millbrae
pins.location_name: Bayside Manor and Marina Vista Park
pins.summary: Becker secured $300,000 in the 2023 state budget for the City of Millbrae to support its Bayside Manor and Marina Vista Park projects, working alongside Assemblymember Diane Papan.

pins.title: $300,000 secured for a youth anti-antisemitism fellowship in Palo Alto
pins.summary: Becker secured $300,000 in the 2023 state budget for the Oshman Family Jewish Community Center in Palo Alto to run its PREP Fellowship, a pilot program preparing teens to counter antisemitism before they head to college.

pins.title: $200,000 secured for a Redwood City youth-opportunity program
pins.summary: Becker secured $200,000 in the 2023 state budget for Redwood City Together's PACE program, which provides mentoring, activities, and support to local 'opportunity youth' who are out of school or work.

pins.title: $1 million secured to fix flood protection for Redwood City mobile home parks
pins.location_name: Redwood City mobile home park flood protection (with OneShoreline)
pins.summary: Becker secured $1 million in the 2023 state budget for Redwood City and the county's OneShoreline agency to repair and reinforce flood protections for mobile home parks that had flooded repeatedly because of undersized, failing pumps.

pins.title: $1 million secured for water recycling in Burlingame
pins.location_name: City of Burlingame wastewater reclamation project
pins.summary: Becker secured $1 million in the 2023 state budget for the City of Burlingame to reclaim wastewater and cut demand for drinking water, helping the city prepare for future droughts.

pins.title: $200,000 secured for solar streetlights and greener infrastructure in Los Altos
pins.location_name: City of Los Altos / GreenTown Los Altos
pins.summary: Becker secured $200,000 in the 2023 state budget for the City of Los Altos, with GreenTown Los Altos, to move toward greener infrastructure and convert streetlights — one of the city's biggest energy users — to solar.

pins.title: Spoke at the groundbreaking for LifeMoves transitional housing in the Baylands
pins.summary: Senator Becker spoke at the October 2023 groundbreaking for a LifeMoves modular transitional-housing project in the Palo Alto Baylands that will serve about 100 people at a time. Becker has worked to secure state Homekey funding for projects like it.

pins.title: ALAS named Senate District 13 Nonprofit of the Year
pins.summary: Senator Becker named Ayudando Latinos A Soñar (ALAS) his 2023 California Nonprofit of the Year. The Half Moon Bay nonprofit advocates for farmworkers and provides social services, and was recognized for supporting the community after the January 2023 Half Moon Bay farmworker shootings.

pins.title: Convened a community meeting with Caltrans on El Camino Real road repairs
pins.summary: Senator Becker and Assemblymember Marc Berman convened a community meeting with Caltrans at the Mountain View Community Center on the status of El Camino Real roadway improvements. Caltrans representatives discussed pothole repair and an upcoming pavement rehabilitation project. Staff from Mountain View, Los Altos, and Palo Alto were on hand to answer residents' questions.

pins.title: Opened a new District 13 field office in Menlo Park
pins.summary: Senator Becker opened his relocated district office in Menlo Park with a public open house and a ribbon cutting alongside the Chamber San Mateo County. Residents were invited to drop in, see the new office, and meet the staff who handle casework for the district. This remains the district office for Senate District 13.

pins.title: Held a community coffee with residents in San Bruno
pins.summary: Senator Becker held a "Java with Josh" community coffee at Mazra Mediterranean Restaurant in San Bruno, joined by San Bruno Mayor Rico Medina. The informal gathering was one in a series held around the Peninsula so residents could hear about his legislative work and share local concerns.

pins.title: Convened a community meeting in Woodside on the Highway 84 landslide closure
pins.summary: After a landslide closed State Route 84 through Woodside, Senator Becker convened a community meeting at Woodside's Independence Hall so residents could hear directly from Caltrans about the repair. He was joined by Assemblymember Marc Berman, County Supervisor Ray Mueller and Woodside Mayor Chris Shaw.

pins.title: Marched in the Hillsborough Memorial Day Parade
pins.summary: Senator Becker took part in the Town of Hillsborough's annual Memorial Day Parade and spoke at the observance ceremony that follows it. The parade runs from near Town Hall along Floribunda and Eucalyptus avenues to North School.

pins.title: Honored a Navy veteran at a Hillsborough ceremony
pins.summary: At a Veterans Day ceremony in Hillsborough, Senator Becker honored Dr. Joseph Haggerty for his service in the Navy. Dr. Haggerty later served as head team physician for the San Francisco 49ers.

pins.title: Held a community coffee at the Belmont Library
pins.summary: Senator Becker held one of his "Java with Josh" community coffees at the Belmont Library, where more than 50 residents came to ask him questions about state issues. Belmont Mayor Julia Mates and County Supervisor Ray Mueller joined him.

pins.title: Spoke to the Los Altos Hills Youth Commission
pins.summary: Senator Becker spoke to the Los Altos Hills Youth Commission about his path into public service and politics. It was a chance for the town's young people to hear directly from their state senator. The source does not name a venue, so the pin sits at Town Hall, where the commission meets.

pins.title: Toured Pie Ranch and Cascade Ranch to see coastside farming practices
pins.summary: Senator Becker toured Pie Ranch and the neighboring Cascade Ranch in Pescadero to see how coastside farms are working more sustainably. The visit covered land stewardship and the electric farm equipment local growers are now sharing.

pins.title: Visited the All Five early learning center in Menlo Park
pins.summary: Senator Becker stopped by All Five in Menlo Park to see the early education work the center is doing. He met teachers, administrators and students, and took part in story time with the children.

pins.title: $4.45 million secured to convert a parking lot into a downtown park
pins.location_name: New downtown public park (former parking lot)
pins.summary: Becker secured $4.45 million in the state budget to help turn a downtown parking lot into a new public park next to the Redwood City Public Library. He presented the funding to city officials in November 2022.

pins.title: $2 million secured to replace the Newell Road Bridge
pins.location_name: Newell Road Bridge (over San Francisquito Creek)
pins.summary: Becker secured $2 million in the state budget to help replace the Newell Road Bridge, an aging span classified as functionally obsolete that links Palo Alto and East Palo Alto over San Francisquito Creek.

pins.title: $4.5 million secured for home electrification in Menlo Park
pins.location_name: City of Menlo Park electrification program
pins.summary: Becker secured $4.5 million in the state budget to help Menlo Park electrify homes and municipal buildings — replacing gas appliances with electric ones — starting in the Belle Haven neighborhood. He presented the funds to the City Council in November 2022.

pins.title: $1 million secured for entrepreneurship and job training in South San Francisco
pins.summary: Becker secured $1 million in the 2022 state budget for South San Francisco to fund programs across North San Mateo County that support entrepreneurship, help small businesses, and provide job training for unemployed and underemployed residents.

pins.title: $500,000 secured for a construction-trades apprenticeship program in San Mateo County
pins.location_name: San Mateo County Union Community Alliance
pins.summary: Becker secured $500,000 in the 2022 state budget for the San Mateo County Union Community Alliance's 20-week Trades Introduction Program, which helps women, people of color, and other underrepresented residents enter green construction trades, with support such as transportation and childcare.

pins.title: Funding secured to replace the synthetic turf field at Fair Oaks School
pins.summary: As part of $4.45 million Senator Becker secured for Redwood City in the 2022 state budget, the funding helps the city replace the synthetic turf field at Fair Oaks School, in an underserved neighborhood without ready access to parks.

pins.title: Funding secured to replace the synthetic turf field at Hawes Park
pins.summary: As part of $4.45 million Senator Becker secured for Redwood City in the 2022 state budget, the funding helps the city replace the synthetic turf field at Hawes Park, in an underserved neighborhood without ready access to parks.

pins.title: Named Project Safety Net of Palo Alto the 13th Senate District's Nonprofit of the Year
pins.summary: Senator Becker named Project Safety Net of Palo Alto, a nonprofit working to prevent teen suicides and support youth mental health, as the 13th Senate District's 2022 Nonprofit of the Year, honoring the organization at a celebration at the state Capitol.

pins.title: Named Reach and Teach the 2022 Small Business of the Year for Senate District 13
pins.summary: Senator Becker named the independent San Mateo bookstore Reach and Teach, owned by Craig Wiesner and Derrick Kikuchi, the 2022 Small Business of the Year for the 13th Senate District, recognizing its focus on peacemaking, social justice, and sustainability. The business was honored at the California Small Business Association's annual celebration.

pins.title: Collected winter coats for East Palo Alto families at a Palo Alto community gathering
pins.location_name: King Plaza, Palo Alto City Hall
pins.summary: Senator Becker held a community gathering at King Plaza in front of Palo Alto City Hall with Palo Alto Mayor Pat Burt and City Manager Ed Shikada. New and gently used winter coats were collected at the event for a coat drive run with the Ecumenical Hunger Program in East Palo Alto. It was the second consecutive year he partnered with the organization on the drive.

pins.title: Held a Coastside community coffee at Mac Dutra Park in Half Moon Bay
pins.summary: Senator Becker held an outdoor "Java with Josh" community coffee at Mac Dutra Park in Half Moon Bay, focused on the Coastside. Residents were invited to hear about his work in the Legislature and raise local issues. The announcement described the gathering as continuing the tradition of his predecessor's community coffee events.

pins.title: Authored SB 893, which let San Mateo County's community colleges go tuition-free
pins.location_name: San Mateo County Community College District
pins.summary: Senator Becker authored SB 893, a pilot that allows the San Mateo County Community College District to use local funds to reduce or eliminate tuition and fees through July 1, 2028. After it was signed, the district's board voted to eliminate tuition, fees, books and educational materials for all students starting January 1, 2023. The district serves roughly 30,000 students across three campuses.

pins.title: Held a press conference in San Bruno urging the Governor to sign the free-prison-calls bill
pins.summary: Senator Becker held a press conference at the San Francisco County Jail in San Bruno urging the Governor to sign his Keep Families Connected Act, which makes phone calls from state prisons and juvenile halls free. He was joined by community advocates and law enforcement; the Governor signed the bill later that month.

pins.title: Presented a Senate certificate marking the Pigeon Point Light Station's 150th anniversary
pins.location_name: Pigeon Point Light Station State Historic Park
pins.summary: Senator Becker marked the 150th anniversary of the Pigeon Point Light Station with a Senate Certificate of Recognition. The lighthouse, part of the California State Park system, has guided mariners along the San Mateo County coast since 1872.

pins.title: Named Emily Ann Ramos the 13th Senate District's 2022 Woman of the Year
pins.summary: Senator Becker named Emily Ann Ramos, a Mountain View resident and tenants' rights advocate, the 2022 Woman of the Year for Senate District 13. Ramos works on tenant protections and affordable housing at SV@Home and serves on Mountain View's Rental Housing Committee. The honor was presented in March 2022 to mark Women's History Month.

pins.title: $5 million secured for JobTrain's Center for Economic Mobility in East Palo Alto
pins.summary: Becker secured $5 million in the 2021 state budget to help build JobTrain's new Center for Economic Mobility in East Palo Alto, a facility for job training, workforce services, and youth and early-childhood programs. The state funds were matched by a grant from the Emerson Collective.

pins.title: $500,000 secured to repair the Pacifica Pier
pins.summary: Becker secured $500,000 in the 2021 state budget to repair the Pacifica Pier, fixing damaged railings and deterioration so the popular fishing and recreation pier could stay open to the public.

pins.title: Named Bistro Vida the 13th Senate District's Small Business of the Year
pins.summary: Senator Becker named Bistro Vida, a downtown Menlo Park restaurant owned by Ali El Safy, as the 13th Senate District's Small Business of the Year and honored it at the California Small Business Association's annual Small Business Day in Sacramento. Becker credited the restaurant with helping keep downtown Menlo Park vibrant through the pandemic, including a parklet that became part of a community plaza.

pins.title: Championed statewide Ruby Bridges Walk to School Day at Martin Elementary
pins.summary: Senator Becker introduced Senate Resolution 59, which the Senate passed unanimously, proclaiming November 14 as Ruby Bridges Walk to School Day in California, an effort driven by fifth-graders at Martin Elementary School in South San Francisco. Becker joined students, teachers and families at the school to celebrate the state's first observance.

pins.title: $8 million secured for Mountain View's 'Lot 12' affordable housing project
pins.summary: Senator Becker supported a state budget that included $8 million for Mountain View's "Lot 12" affordable housing project in the downtown area. The project was planned to include roughly 120 affordable homes, with some set aside for rapid rehousing.

pins.title: Authored SB 640, letting small cities pool state road funds — an idea that started in Belmont
pins.summary: Senator Becker authored SB 640, signed in July 2021, which lets California cities and counties pool state transportation funds for road maintenance projects that benefit neighboring communities. The press release credits Belmont as the city where the idea originated. Burlingame, San Carlos, San Mateo and South San Francisco were also named as cities that could use it.

pins.title: $1 million secured for The Big Lift early-literacy program in San Mateo County
pins.location_name: San Mateo County Office of Education (The Big Lift)
pins.summary: In the 2021 state budget Senator Becker secured $1 million for The Big Lift, San Mateo County's early-literacy initiative. The money funded a five-week full-day summer STEAM and literacy program for 1,200 low-income kindergarten-through-third-grade students, plus an evidence-based literacy program for 720 low-income preschoolers during the 2021-22 school year. The Big Lift is a partnership of San Mateo County, the San Mateo County Office of Education and the Silicon Valley Community Foundation.

statewide.title: Authored SB 913 to lower electricity costs using customer-owned resources
statewide.summary: The California State Senate passed SB 913, authored by Senator Becker, to let customer-owned resources like home batteries, electric vehicles, and smart thermostats compete fairly with traditional power sources to provide grid reliability at lower cost. The bill removes barriers to participation, allows enrollment of multiple devices, and permits compensation for energy exported to the grid. It passed the Senate and moved to the Assembly.

statewide.title: California Senate passed SB 905 on utility accountability and electricity affordability
statewide.summary: The California State Senate passed SB 905, authored by Senator Becker, which aims to strengthen oversight of investor-owned utilities and control long-term electricity costs for ratepayers. The bill ties utility executive compensation to rates, sets performance standards, and reduces excessive utility profits on certain lower-risk investments.

statewide.title: Authored SB 1282, the Battery Integration and Grid Reliability Act
statewide.summary: Senator Becker authored SB 1282, which the Senate Committee on Energy, Utilities, and Communications approved. The bill enables vehicle-to-grid and vehicle-to-home technologies so electric vehicle batteries can support the grid and power homes during outages, aiming to lower electricity costs and improve reliability.

statewide.title: Helped double state funding for Bay Area shoreline flood protection ($102 million)
statewide.summary: As Bay Area Caucus chair, Becker helped secure a doubling of state funding — to $102 million — for coastal and bay shoreline flood-protection projects across the Bay Area in the 2025 budget, in a county considered California's most vulnerable to shoreline flooding.

statewide.title: Authored SB 306, signed into law to streamline prior authorization for care
statewide.summary: The Governor signed Senator Becker's SB 306, the Defending Physicians Decisions Act. The law requires that health care services approved by insurers at least 90 percent of the time be placed on a list exempt from prior authorization, cutting delays and paperwork for routine treatments.

statewide.title: Authored bill to cut housing fees near transit, passed by Senate
statewide.summary: The California State Senate passed SB 358, authored by Senator Becker, which requires at least a 50 percent reduction in vehicular traffic impact fees for housing built near public transit. The bill aims to lower construction and rental costs and encourage infill development.

statewide.title: Authored SB 541 to create energy affordability through demand flexibility
statewide.summary: The Legislature approved SB 541, authored by Senator Becker, which directs state agencies to set targets for load-shifting and capture 7,500 MW of demand flexibility by 2030 using batteries, smart EV charging, thermostats, and other distributed energy resources. It requires annual public reporting on each electricity supplier's progress. The bill passed both houses and headed to the Governor.

statewide.title: Authored SB 285 to strengthen carbon removal standards
statewide.summary: The Senate Committee on Environmental Quality approved SB 285, authored by Senator Becker, which establishes rigorous standards for carbon dioxide removal and offsets used to meet California's net-zero goals. The bill requires durable carbon storage, limits biomass feedstocks to waste materials, excludes enhanced oil recovery, and mandates transparent reporting.

statewide.title: Authored SB 254, signed into law as major energy affordability bill
statewide.summary: Governor Newsom signed SB 254, authored by Senator Becker, a wide-ranging energy affordability and wildfire law. It requires utilities to securitize $6 billion in wildfire safety investments to save ratepayers more than $300 million annually, expands low-cost public financing for transmission, strengthens oversight of utility profits and wildfire mitigation spending, and extends the state Wildfire Fund through 2045.

statewide.title: Introduced SB 468, the Artificial Intelligence Security and Protection Act
statewide.summary: Senator Becker introduced SB 468, which requires businesses deploying high-risk AI systems that process personal information to maintain a comprehensive security program, including risk assessments, employee training, third-party oversight, and incident response plans. Violations would be treated as deceptive trade practices under California's Unfair Competition Law.

statewide.title: Authored law (SB 822) protecting unclaimed virtual currency, signed by Governor
statewide.summary: Governor Newsom signed SB 822, authored by Senator Becker, modernizing California's Unclaimed Property Law to define how virtual currencies like Bitcoin and Ethereum are handled. Abandoned crypto is now safeguarded by the State Controller's Office and treated like stocks until reunited with rightful owners. The law takes effect January 1, 2026.

statewide.title: Authored SB 606 to move California toward ending unsheltered homelessness
statewide.summary: Senator Becker's SB 606 passed the Senate. The bill requires Homeless Housing, Assistance, and Prevention recipients to assess and plan the resources needed to bring all unsheltered individuals indoors, promotes regional collaboration, and encourages tools like the Shelter Crisis Act to expedite housing.

statewide.title: Authored law expanding mobile telehealth for farmworkers (SB 338)
statewide.summary: Senator Becker authored SB 338, signed into law in October 2025, which establishes the Virtual Health Hub for Rural Communities Pilot Program within the Department of Health Care Services. The pilot awards grants to community-based partnerships to deploy virtual health hubs delivering telehealth and preventive care to farmworkers in two rural communities. The bill grew out of the Senate District 13 'There Ought to be a Law' competition and builds on the ALAS Farmworker Equity Express mobile clinic.

statewide.title: Authored the Defending Californians' Data Act signed into law
statewide.summary: Governor Newsom signed SB 361, the Defending Californians' Data Act, authored by Senator Becker. The law strengthens consumer protections and increases transparency around data brokers who sell sensitive personal information such as citizenship status, biometric data, and government-issued ID numbers.

statewide.title: Authored SB 540 to expand California's regional energy market
statewide.summary: Senator Becker is an author of SB 540, the Pathways bill establishing a framework for regional energy cooperation across the West while preserving California's authority over its grid and climate goals. The Senate Energy, Utilities and Communications Committee approved it unanimously, 17-0, in April 2025.

statewide.title: Authored SB 1254, the FRESH Act, passed by the Assembly
statewide.summary: Senator Becker authored SB 1254, the FRESH Act, which passed the Assembly with a unanimous, bipartisan vote. The bill lets incarcerated individuals pre-apply for CalFresh benefits 90 days before release to support successful reentry and reduce food insecurity, tapping underutilized federal funding at no additional state cost.

statewide.title: Authored SB 1120, the Physicians Make Decisions Act, signed into law
statewide.summary: Governor Newsom signed Senator Becker's SB 1120, the Physicians Make Decisions Act. The law requires that any denial, delay, or modification of health care services based on medical necessity be made by a licensed physician or qualified provider rather than an artificial intelligence algorithm.

statewide.title: Authored the Interim Housing Act (SB 1395), signed into law
statewide.summary: Senator Becker authored SB 1395, the Interim Housing Act, signed into law by Governor Newsom. The law expands access to interim housing statewide by clarifying that relocatable non-congregate interim housing is eligible for streamlined zoning, expediting local approvals, extending existing streamlining authorities, and freeing up state funding for interim housing.

statewide.title: Authored SB 942, the California AI Transparency Act, signed into law
statewide.summary: Governor Newsom signed into law SB 942, the California Artificial Intelligence Transparency Act, authored by Senator Becker. The law requires large generative AI providers to label AI-generated content and to make a free AI-detection tool available so consumers can determine whether content was AI-generated.

statewide.title: Authored SB 1374 to give solar customers fair credit for self-consumption
statewide.summary: The Senate Committee on Energy, Utilities and Communications passed SB 1374, authored by Senator Becker, which restores the ability for utility customers with on-site solar generation split across separate meters, such as schools, apartment buildings, and farms, to be fairly credited for self-consuming that electricity. The bill directs the CPUC to update tariffs so multiple-metered customers get equal treatment.

statewide.title: Authored law creating Mexican Repatriation memorial (SB 537)
statewide.summary: Senator Becker co-authored SB 537, signed into law, which authorizes a designated non-profit foundation to plan, construct, and maintain a statue in Los Angeles commemorating victims of the 1930s Mexican Repatriation program, at no cost to the state. Becker and Senate Majority Leader Lena Gonzalez launched the associated Mexican Repatriation Memorial Project. The bill was inspired by a high school student's research paper.

statewide.title: Authored SB 1206 to incentivize a next-generation battery manufacturing hub
statewide.summary: Senator Becker authored SB 1206, which passed the Senate Committee on Energy, Utilities and Communications and would incentivize a first-of-its-kind battery manufacturing facility for next-generation batteries. The bill authorizes GO-Biz to develop a public-private partnership to plan a battery manufacturing hub, aiming to create high-paying union jobs and advance clean energy goals.

statewide.title: Authored bill making childcare workers eligible for subsidized childcare
statewide.summary: The Senate Committee on Human Services unanimously approved SB 1307, authored by Senator Becker, which makes early childhood education workers eligible for state-subsidized child care to help grow the ECE workforce. The bill was sponsored by All Five, winner of the district's 'There Ought to be a Law' contest.

statewide.title: Authored SB 1018 to foster green hydrogen and cut emissions
statewide.summary: The Senate approved SB 1018, authored by Senator Becker, and sent it to the Assembly. The bill allows hydrogen producers and industrial customers to be supplied clean electricity directly from large solar or wind farms rather than the grid, to foster a green hydrogen industry and reduce greenhouse gas emissions in the industrial sector.

statewide.title: Authored the FIRE Act (SB 1060) to reward wildfire risk reduction in insurance
statewide.summary: Senator Becker authored SB 1060, the Fire Insurance Risk Evaluation Act, requiring property insurers to account for wildfire mitigation such as home hardening, defensible space, and fuel reduction in their underwriting models. The Senate Insurance Committee passed the bill in April 2024.

statewide.title: Authored SJR 14 urging Congress to close a deferred-compensation tax loophole
statewide.summary: The California Senate passed Senator Becker's Senate Joint Resolution 14, which calls on Congress to establish a cap on deferred compensation for high-income earners. The resolution was prompted by a tax loophole that could allow athletes such as Shohei Ohtani to defer income and avoid substantial state taxes.

statewide.title: Authored law barring AI as the sole basis for denying medically necessary treatment
statewide.summary: Senator Becker authored legislation prohibiting artificial intelligence from being used as the sole determiner for denying medically necessary treatments to patients.

statewide.title: Authored law creating an AI Workgroup in Education
statewide.summary: Senator Becker authored legislation creating an AI Workgroup in Education to guide the responsible use of artificial intelligence in California classrooms.

statewide.title: Co-authored Proposition 4, the state climate bond
statewide.summary: Senator Becker co-authored Proposition 4, the California climate bond approved by voters, which funds forward-looking investments in climate resilience and adaptation. The bond's allocations fund coastal and flood protection projects benefiting the Bay Area.

statewide.title: Authored SB 1223 (2024), the first-in-the-nation neural data privacy law
statewide.summary: Governor Newsom signed Senator Becker's SB 1223 into law in September 2024. It was the first law in the nation to treat brain and nervous-system data as sensitive personal information, so companies must get a person's consent before collecting or selling it. Californians can now tell a company that their neural data is not for sale.

statewide.title: Secured $1.8 million so people leaving prison receive their full release allowance
statewide.summary: California gives people $200 when they leave state prison, and the corrections department had been deducting transportation and clothing costs from it, leaving some with under $120. Senator Becker negotiated $1.8 million in the state budget to stop those deductions. The change applies statewide and affects roughly 10,000 people a year.

statewide.title: $500,000 secured toward the 90-mile Ohlone-Portolá Heritage Trail
statewide.summary: Becker secured $500,000 in the 2023 state budget toward creating the roughly 90-mile Ohlone-Portolá Heritage Trail, which would trace a historic route across San Mateo County. Because it spans the whole county, it's listed here rather than as a single map pin.

statewide.title: Authored SB 410 to speed grid interconnection
statewide.summary: Governor Newsom signed Senator Becker's SB 410, which addresses delayed interconnection improvements by holding utilities such as PG&E accountable to more quickly connect homes and businesses to the electric grid.

statewide.title: Authored SB 448 on least-restrictive alternatives for youth detention
statewide.summary: Governor Newsom signed Senator Becker's SB 448, which ensures youth will be considered for the least restrictive alternatives to detention regardless of their county of residence.

statewide.title: Authored SB 762 to strengthen county jail facility standards
statewide.summary: Senator Becker authored SB 762, unanimously approved by the Assembly Public Safety Committee. The bill requires the Board of State and Community Corrections to update jail facility standards with specific procedures to ensure incarcerated individuals are alive and well, and to create a consistent statewide protocol across jail facilities.

statewide.title: Authored SB 48 to cut carbon emissions in large buildings
statewide.summary: Governor Newsom signed Senator Becker's SB 48, which cuts carbon emissions in large and older buildings.

statewide.title: Authored SB 49 to put solar and clean energy alongside highways
statewide.summary: Governor Newsom signed Senator Becker's SB 49, which incentivizes solar and clean energy projects alongside California highways.

statewide.title: Authored SB 420 to accelerate electric grid distribution upgrades
statewide.summary: The Legislature passed SB 420, authored by Senator Becker, and sent it to the Governor. The bill accelerates approvals for upgrading small, critical distribution lines needed to move energy where it is needed as part of modernizing California's electric grid.

statewide.title: Authored SB 474 to reduce prison canteen markups
statewide.summary: Governor Newsom signed Senator Becker's SB 474, which reduces the markup on everyday necessities such as hygiene products, food and health supplements sold in prison canteen stores.

statewide.title: Authored SB 341 to unlock state funding for affordable housing
statewide.summary: Governor Newsom signed Senator Becker's SB 341, which unlocks state funding for affordable housing.

statewide.title: Authored SB 362, the DELETE Act, signed into law
statewide.summary: Governor Newsom signed Senator Becker's SB 362, the DELETE Act, creating a first-in-the-nation one-stop way for Californians to require data brokers to delete their personal information free of charge. The law becomes operative in 2026 to allow time for implementation.

statewide.title: Authored bill to boost funding for child health and safety programs
statewide.summary: SB 608, authored by Senator Becker, passed the Senate Transportation Committee 14-0. The bill updates the Kids' Plates specialty license plate program by raising fees and changing the distribution formula so funding for local child health and safety programs is spread equitably across all 58 counties.

statewide.title: Authored SB 485 to protect election workers from harassment
statewide.summary: Governor Newsom signed Senator Becker's SB 485, which protects election workers and volunteers from harassment.

statewide.title: Authored SB 755 to create a one-stop energy incentive application
statewide.summary: Through his 'Ought to Be A Law' contest, Senator Becker selected a constituent's proposal and authored SB 755 (CLEAR), which would require the California Energy Commission to build a single online application for residents to check eligibility for and apply to energy efficiency and building decarbonization incentive programs currently split across multiple agencies.

statewide.title: Authored SB 719, the Law Enforcement Communications Transparency Act
statewide.summary: Senator Becker introduced SB 719, the Law Enforcement Communications Transparency Act, which would require law enforcement agencies that encrypt all radio communications to grant media access to review those communications within 30 days, restoring public and press access to police radio. The bill is co-sponsored by the California News Publishers Association and California Broadcasters Association.

statewide.title: Authored a 2023 bill, passed by the Legislature, to keep cross-county public meetings open by teleconference
statewide.summary: Some local agencies in Senate District 13 span more than a hundred miles across two counties. That makes it costly for residents to attend their meetings in person, so Senator Becker wrote a bill letting those cross-county agencies keep meeting by teleconference. The Legislature approved it in September 2023 and sent it to the Governor.

statewide.title: Authored SB 1203, California Zero, signed into law
statewide.summary: Senator Becker authored SB 1203, known as California Zero, which was signed into law. It requires the state to develop a plan to get its buildings, vehicle fleet, and electricity usage to net zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2035.

statewide.title: Authored SB 1158 requiring disclosure of clean-power grid status
statewide.summary: Senator Becker authored SB 1158, which was signed into law and requires power companies such as PG&E to disclose when the electricity grid is running on clean power.

statewide.title: Authored SB 887 requiring 15-year energy resource projections
statewide.summary: Senator Becker authored SB 887, which was signed into law and requires the state's energy agencies to provide 15-year projections of energy resources and demands so California can ensure transmission facilities are built to meet clean energy goals.

statewide.title: Authored SB 1112 for low-cost building decarbonization financing
statewide.summary: The Legislature passed Senator Becker's SB 1112, which supports equitable financing so more people can afford to decarbonize their homes and buildings by eliminating large up-front costs and letting owners pay over time. It was sent to the Governor for review.

statewide.title: Authored the Keep Families Connected Act (SB 1008) making prison phone calls free
statewide.summary: Governor Newsom signed Senator Becker's SB 1008, the Keep Families Connected Act, into law. Effective January 1, 2023, it eliminates per-minute charges and connection fees for phone calls to and from people in California state prisons and state and local juvenile detention facilities.

statewide.title: Authored SB 1223 (2022) requiring mental-health diversion for eligible defendants
statewide.summary: Senator Becker authored SB 1223, signed into law effective January 1, 2023. It requires a court to divert a defendant into a mental health program if the defendant has a diagnosed mental disorder that was a significant factor in the commission of the crime.

statewide.title: Authored SB 1117 letting public-defender grants fund wrap-around services
statewide.summary: Senator Becker authored SB 1117, signed into law effective January 1, 2023. It allows the State Public Defender's office to provide grants to counties that can be used not only for legal defense but also to help defendants access services such as CalFresh, MediCal, transit passes, mental health assistance, and housing help.

statewide.title: Authored California Employee Ownership Act (SB 1407)
statewide.summary: Governor Newsom signed Senator Becker's SB 1407, the California Employee Ownership Act, into law. It creates a hub within the Governor's Office of Business and Economic Development (GO-Biz) to help business owners and workers learn about and transition to employee-owned models such as ESOPs and worker cooperatives. The bill passed both houses unanimously and took effect January 1, 2023.

statewide.title: Authored SB 948 freeing up funds for affordable housing construction
statewide.summary: Senator Becker authored SB 948, signed into law effective January 1, 2023. It eliminates duplicative financial reserve requirements on affordable housing developers, freeing an estimated $40 million to build more affordable housing units.

statewide.title: Authored SB 1346 enabling a regional free pharmacy for surplus medications
statewide.summary: Senator Becker authored SB 1346, signed by the Governor, which allows Santa Clara, San Mateo, and San Francisco counties to launch a regional free pharmacy that repurposes surplus unused, unopened, and unexpired medications to fill free prescriptions for people in financial hardship. The bill passed both houses unanimously.

statewide.title: Authored SB 1419 to protect patient medical records
statewide.summary: The Legislature passed Senator Becker's SB 1419, which provides new protections so patients receive sensitive information about their clinical laboratory tests and imaging scans in the manner that works best for them. It was sent to the Governor for review.

statewide.title: Authored law expanding civil court fee waivers for low-income Californians (SB 355)
statewide.summary: Senator Becker introduced SB 355 to expand eligibility for waivers of civil court filing fees, raising the income cap from 125% to 200% of the federal poverty level and extending waivers to WIC and unemployment recipients. Its provisions were absorbed into budget bill AB 199 and took effect when signed into law on June 30, 2022. The measure was inspired by Community Legal Services in East Palo Alto and other legal aid groups.

statewide.title: Authored SB 504, signed into law to expand voter registration access
statewide.summary: Acting Governor Eleni Kounalakis signed Senator Becker's SB 504 into law, ensuring equal access to voter registration for overseas military personnel and people living with disabilities. The law also notifies formerly justice-involved Californians when they are eligible to re-register and clarifies that vote-by-mail ballots are mailed to all voters without an application.

statewide.title: Introduced SB 1094 to remove barriers to affordable housing funding
statewide.summary: Senator Becker introduced SB 1094, which ensures affordable housing developers cannot be blocked from state funding when a city or county is out of compliance with housing element law, and provides RHNA credit incentives for interim housing, home-sharing programs, and converting market-rate units to affordable housing.

statewide.title: Authored SB 1248, the Minor League Baseball Players' Bill of Rights
statewide.summary: Senator Becker introduced SB 1248 to establish the Minor League Baseball Players' Bill of Rights, which would subject affiliated minor league players in California to state labor laws, limit initial player contracts to four years, and guarantee players' name, image, and likeness rights without retaliation.

statewide.title: Authored SB 775, the BESTT Practices Act 2.0, signed into law
statewide.summary: Governor Newsom signed Senator Becker's SB 775, the BESTT Practices Act 2.0, a criminal justice reform. The law clarifies that voluntary manslaughter and attempted murder convictions are eligible for resentencing relief under SB 1437, assisting people excluded by narrow appellate interpretations. It took effect January 1, 2022.

statewide.title: Authored SB 591 to enable intergenerational affordable housing
statewide.summary: Governor Newsom signed SB 591, authored by Senator Becker, which enables affordable housing developers to build intergenerational housing for seniors and transition-age foster youth by using tax credits for financing. The law removed a barrier that previously prohibited mixing these populations in tax-credit-financed buildings.

statewide.title: Authored SB 503, signed into law, setting a statewide standard for mail-in ballot signature verification
statewide.summary: Governor Newsom signed Senator Becker's SB 503, which implements a statewide standard for signature verification of mail-in ballots, requires timely outreach to voters whose ballots are rejected, and requires periodic reporting on rejections. The law codifies and builds on emergency measures used in the November 2020 election and took effect January 1, 2022.

statewide.title: Authored landmark SB 596 targeting net-zero emissions from cement
statewide.summary: Governor Newsom signed Senator Becker's SB 596, making California the first state to directly target greenhouse gas emissions from cement and the first California bill in any sector to focus on net-zero emissions. The law requires a comprehensive strategy to achieve net-zero-emission cement used in California no later than 2045.

statewide.title: Authored SB 779 expanding earn-and-learn job training, signed into law
statewide.summary: Governor Newsom signed Senator Becker's SB 779, which expands 'earn and learn' job-training opportunities for veterans, unhoused people, those exiting the justice system, and others facing employment barriers by making employment social enterprises and worker cooperatives eligible for earn-and-learn funding consideration.

statewide.title: Authored SB 68, signed into law to ease building electrification
statewide.summary: Governor Newsom signed Senator Becker's SB 68, which supports building electrification by reducing costs, permitting delays, and other barriers for property owners replacing fossil-fuel equipment. The law directs the California Energy Commission to develop best practices and took effect January 1, 2022.
